items.title: 2.7/3.0 Nano EcoBoost intake valves may break
items.summary: Broken intake valves can cause engine failure; dealers run an engine cycle test and replace the engine as needed (Ford 24S55).

items.title: Rear shock reservoirs can corrode and detach
items.summary: Dealers replace the rear shocks (Ford 25S01); owner letters mailed August 2025.

items.title: Molded-in-color hardtop roof panels can separate
items.summary: Sections of the outer roof panel can detach; dealers will inspect and replace tops, with the remedy expected November 2026 (Ford 26S32).

items.title: Engine-compartment wiring harness can short
items.summary: Dealers add protective sheathing; phased campaign, Raptors first, then all other Broncos from about September 2026.

items.title: Steering gear internal damage
items.summary: Increased steering effort or wheel lock-up possible; owners told not to drive until the steering gear is replaced.

items.title: Transmission-to-transfer-case joint misaligned after a previous repair
items.summary: Can wear the output and input splines; dealers inspect and replace the transmission and transfer case as needed.

items.title: Front upper control-arm ball-joint nut loose or missing
items.summary: The upper arm can separate from the knuckle; dealers inspect and tighten, or replace the ball joint and knuckle.

items.title: Front lower control-arm fasteners not tightened
items.summary: The arm can detach from the frame; owners told not to drive until it has been inspected.

items.title: Fender flares may detach
items.summary: Dealers inspect and repair or replace the flares.

items.title: Windshield not properly bonded
items.summary: The windshield could detach in a crash; dealers remove and reinstall it.

items.title: Transmission park pawl damaged in assembly
items.summary: Rollaway risk; dealers replace the transmission.

items.title: Low-pressure fuel pump may fail
items.summary: Can stall the engine; PCM software update on the Bronco.

items.title: Passenger airbag vent may open early
Engine may fail (2025–26)
items.summary: Dealers will replace the long block; remedy expected November 2026.

timeline.change: Production starts June 14, 2021 at Michigan Assembly. 2.3 (manual or auto) and 2.7 (auto) EcoBoost; Base, Big Bend, Black Diamond, Outer Banks, Badlands, Wildtrak and First Edition; Sasquatch package. CarGurus says to steer clear of 2021–22: the year with the most recalls, including 2.7 intake valves (24V-635), molded-in-color roof panels and airbags.

Bronco Raptor (four-door, 3.0 twin-turbo V6, 37s) and the four-door-only Everglades edition arrive. Still inside the 2.7 valve recall, and 2021–22 molded-in-color roof panels are recalled in 2026; CarGurus says to avoid it.

Heritage Edition and Heritage Limited Edition arrive, both with a painted top instead of the molded-in-color one. CarGurus' pick of the generation, with fewer complaints than 2021–22, provided the recalls are done.
Badlands and Sasquatch trucks get the Wildtrak's HOSS 3.0 steering gear. Chinese-market Broncos go on sale (2.3, four-door). Last year of the Wildtrak trim.

Full HOSS 3.0 (Fox 2.5 internal-bypass shocks, Raptor steering rack, stronger tie rods) optional on Badlands. Painted hardtops in Oxford White, Shadow Black or body color. Two-door Stroppe Edition ($77,665). Front control-arm fastener recalls on early builds.
The Stroppe Edition moves to the four-door, at $69,995.

identify.intro: Sixth-gen trims are mostly about suspension, tires and tops. Aftermarket 35s and badges are easy to add, so check what you're actually buying.

items.head: Real Sasquatch
items.body: 315/70R17 tires on 17x8.5, +30 mm wheels and 4.7 axle gears. Standard wheels are +55 mm. Confirm with the window sticker or build data.

items.head: Bronco Raptor
items.body: Four-door only. 'FORD' spelled across the grille (other trims say BRONCO), an 85.7-inch-wide body with extra marker lights, 37-inch tires, Fox suspension and a 3.0 V6 with 418 hp.

items.head: Suspension level
items.body: Badlands (and Sasquatch) trucks have position-sensitive Bilstein dampers (HOSS 2.0) and a hydraulic front sway-bar disconnect. Wildtrak trucks have Fox dampers (HOSS 3.0). From 2025, Badlands buyers could add the full HOSS 3.0 package.

items.head: First Edition
items.body: 2021 only: Badlands mechanicals with Wildtrak exterior styling and the Outer Banks interior, and 35s standard.

items.head: Which top
items.body: Original molded-in-color, replacement 'MIC 2.0', or painted (2023 Heritage editions, then optional from 2025). A crazed or delaminated MIC top is a recall and program candidate.

editions.name: First Edition
editions.note: Announced at 3,500 units; Badlands hardware with Wildtrak styling. The first production example sold for $1,075,000 at Barrett-Jackson for charity.

editions.name: Everglades
editions.note: Four-door, Black Diamond-based, with a heavy-duty modular bumper and fender graphics that double as a fording-depth gauge.

editions.name: Stroppe Edition
editions.note: Tribute to Bill Stroppe's Baja Broncos in Code Orange, Oxford White and Atlas Blue. Two-door for 2025 ($77,665), four-door for 2026 ($69,995).
